subject: Fixing factor loading to 1: different results depending on choice

messages.author: fe044bb666cd885d
messages.subject: Fixing factor loading to 1: different results depending on choice
parts: I'm using lavaan and SEM for the first time and I'm confused about fixing certain factor loadings to 1. I tried fixing different observed variables to 1 just to see what happens and actually the results differ immensely. I thought that usually it should not matter and it is ok to use the default = setting the first variable to 1. However, it seems to matter in my dataset. Am I right to understand that this means something is off with my data and it is not really possible to choose which variable to fix a priori? What could I check or change? Thank you in advance!

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Fixing factor loading to 1: different results depending on choice
parts:
The standardized solution and the model-implied moments (thus, the fit statistic) are scale invariant.  However, unstandardized estimates are entirely dependent on the arbitrary scale assigned to the common factor(s), so different indicators lead to different results.  Loadings will be proportionally equivalent regardless of which is fixed to 1, but unfortunately, their SEs (and therefore Wald z tests) are not proportionally equivalent.  Because some indicators are more reliable than others, fixing different ones results in different imprecision of estimation of the remaining estimates.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
